1.explanation:
• TileGroup.tsx / index.js – this component currently only handles name, value, and onChange for tiles; it needs to accept a top-level `required` prop and pass it down to each RadioTile via context/child cloning so you no longer have to repeat `required` on every RadioTile.

• RadioTile.tsx / index.ts – this is where the native `<input type="radio">` sits (hidden visually). It needs to receive the propagated `required` attribute when TileGroup is marked required.

• _tile-group.scss – we need to declare `.bx--tile-group { position: relative; }` so that absolutely-positioned inputs inside it will be placed relative to the entire group container.

• _tile.scss – this is where `.bx--tile-input` is defined. We need to adjust its positioning rules (e.g. `bottom: 0; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%);`) so that the (invisible) input that triggers the validation bubble sits at the bottom-center of each tile/group rather than defaulting to the top-left corner.
1.bug_scenario:
When you make a TileGroup of RadioTiles required and submit the form without choosing one, the browser’s native validation marker pops up at the top-left of the (invisible) radio input. In React you currently have to put `required` on every RadioTile instead of the TileGroup as a whole, and the hidden `<input>` that triggers the validation bubble is styled/positioned at the wrong place (top-left) instead of bottom-center of the tile or group.

In the two screenshots:
- The first (light) theme shows the yellow “Please select one of these options” callout in the upper-left corner of the tile container.
- The second (dark) theme shows the same misplaced validation bubble.

The goal is 1) allow passing `required` on TileGroup and propagate it to all RadioTile inputs, and 2) update the CSS so that the hidden radio input is positioned bottom-center of the tile group, e.g.: 
```css
.bx--tile-group { position: relative }
.bx--tile-input { bottom: 0; left: 50%; }
```

2.explanation:
1. TileGroup.tsx: This component should accept a `required` prop and propagate it automatically to each underlying radio input, so users can simply mark the group as required rather than each tile.  
2. RadioTile.tsx: This component renders the hidden `<input type=\"radio\" />` and currently only applies `required` when the prop is explicitly passed; it needs to pick up the group-level `required` as well. It also manages the positioning hooks (styles/classes) for that input.  
3. _tile.scss: The CSS for `.bx--tile-group` and `.bx--tile-input` lives here. Adding `position: relative` to `.bx--tile-group` and adjusting `.bx--tile-input` (e.g. `bottom: 0; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%)`) will ensure the native browser validation popup is anchored to the bottom-center of the tile/group rather than the page corner.
2.bug_scenario: The native HTML `<input type="radio">` elements that live under each `RadioTile` aren’t being validated as a group: you currently have to slap a `required` attribute on *every* `RadioTile` rather than being able to mark the entire `TileGroup` as required. In addition, because the invisible radio inputs aren’t absolutely positioned inside a relatively-positioned container, the browser’s native validation bubble appears in the top-left corner of the viewport instead of centered at the bottom of the tiles (see screenshots).
